mainTopic: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's rulings after the חורבן on יום הנף and on accepting עדות החודש all day, and what mistake the לויים made in the שיר when witnesses came late.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question: why did רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbid new grain (חדש) for the whole יום הנף? The answer is that he followed רבי יהודה, who reads 'עד עצם היום הזה' as 'until and including' the day, making it Torah law. A משנה in סוכה seems to show רבי יהודה arguing with him. The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה misunderstood him, and that 'התקין' there means 'he expounded the פסוק and set it as practice.' Then a new משנה begins about עדות החודש on ראש השנה. Originally testimony was accepted all day. After late witnesses caused the לויים to err in the שיר, the deadline became מנחה. After the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי restored all-day testimony. The גמרא asks what the לויים' mistake was: the Sages of בבל say they sang nothing, and רבי זירא says they sang the weekday song. רבי זירא's proof from the word 'שיבוש' is deflected. Then רב אחא בר הונא brings a ברייתא about the ראש השנה songs, whose phrase 'repeats the section' supports the view that the weekday song was sung when the day was in doubt.

steps.title: He followed the view of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbade the whole יום הנף because he followed רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה reads 'עד עצם היום הזה' as including the entire day, as a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said his ruling following the approach of רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה says the verse 'until this very day' means 'until the essence of the day itself.' He also holds that 'until' means 'until and including.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to an earlier question: why did רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbid new grain for the whole day and not just part of it? The answer is that he held like רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads 'עצם היום' as 'the day itself,' and he reads 'עד' as including the day it names. So when there is no עומר offering, the Torah itself forbids חדש for the entire sixteenth of ניסן. After the בית המקדש was destroyed there is no עומר, so the whole day is forbidden by Torah law. That means רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ruling was not an extra stringency.

keyTerms.meaning: the very day itself (the essence of the day)

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the question. The rule about the whole יום הנף becomes a matter of Torah law, not a rabbinic enactment.

phrases.english: He said it according to the approach of Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: 'He' = רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, regarding his ruling on the day of waving.

phrases.english: who said: 'Until this very day' (Vayikra 23:14)
means until the essence of the day itself.
phrases.notes: Not just until dawn of that day.

phrases.english: And he holds: 'until' means until and including.
phrases.notes: So the entire sixteenth is forbidden by Torah law when there is no עומר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the earlier question (on the previous amud) about why the whole day is forbidden.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ruling to a known opinion (רבי יהודה) that makes it Torah law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבן יוחנן בן זכאי added a rabbinic stringency for the whole day.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was following רבי יהודה's reading of the פסוק, under which the whole day is forbidden by Torah law.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה argues with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי agrees with רבי יהודה. It cites a משנה where רבי יהודה seems to argue with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he really hold like him? But he clearly disagrees with him! We learned in a משנה: after the Temple was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי instituted that the entire day of waving should be forbidden. רבי יהודה said: Isn't it already forbidden by the Torah, as it is written, 'until this very day'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 1 by quoting a משנה in מסכת סוכה. There, רבי יהודה seems to object to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה protests, 'Isn't this already Torah law?', then he must think רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant something different, namely a rabbinic rule. That suggests the two disagree. If so, how can we say רבן יוחנן בן זכאי followed רבי יהודה's approach?

keyTerms.meaning: and does he really hold like him?
the day of waving the עומר (16 ניסן)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי יהודה's words as saying the day is permitted. He agrees the day is forbidden. He is only objecting that it is already forbidden by the Torah.

phrases.english: And does he hold like him?
But he clearly disagrees with him,
as we learned in a Mishnah: After the Temple was destroyed,
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted
that the entire day of waving be forbidden.
Rabbi Yehuda said:
But isn't it forbidden by Torah law?
As it is written: 'Until this very day'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּווֹתֵיהּ? וְהָא מְפַלֵּיג פְּלִיג עֲלֵיהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי followed רבי יהודה's approach.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה in סוכה, רבי יהודה objects to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. That shows they disagree, so רבן יוחנן בן זכאי cannot be following רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה misunderstood him
steps.stepSummary: The disagreement is only apparent. רבי יהודה mistakenly thought רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant a rabbinic rule, but he actually meant it as Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it was רבי יהודה who made a mistake. He thought רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was speaking of a rabbinic law. But that is not so; he was speaking of Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says there is no real disagreement: רבי יהודה simply misread what רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה protested only because he assumed the rule was rabbinic. In truth, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant exactly what רבי יהודה holds: a Torah prohibition. So the two actually agree, and Step 1 stands.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הוּא דְּקָא טָעֵי.
phrases.english: There, it is Rabbi Yehuda who erred.

phrases.aramaic: אִיהוּ סָבַר רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: He thought that Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
was speaking of a rabbinic law,
but that is not so; he was speaking of Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הוּא דְּקָא טָעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 2 and defends Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source: the disagreement came from a misunderstanding.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי truly disagree about the nature of the prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree it is Torah law. רבי יהודה only thought רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant a rabbinic rule.

steps.title: But the משנה says 'instituted'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 3. The משנה uses the word 'התקין,' which normally means a rabbinic enactment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 3 by pointing to the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'התקין' is the usual word for a rabbinic תקנה. If רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was only stating Torah law, why would the משנה say he 'instituted' it? So רבי יהודה seems to have understood him correctly.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'instituted'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 3 based on the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant a Torah law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'התקין' signals a rabbinic enactment. That contradicts the idea that he was only stating Torah law.

steps.title: Instituted means he expounded and set the practice
steps.stepSummary: 'התקין' here means that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי expounded the פסוק and established it as the practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'instituted' mean? He expounded the verse and established the practice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the wording challenge and closes this section. 'Instituted' does not mean he created a new rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the בית המקדש stood, people could eat חדש right after the עומר was brought, so this law never came up in practice. After the destruction, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי taught the Torah reading of the פסוק and set it as the new practice. That is why the משנה calls it 'התקין,' even though it is Torah law.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this sugya, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's rule that all of יום הנף is forbidden is Torah law, following רבי יהודה ('עד ועד בכלל'). The word 'התקין' only means he expounded the פסוק and made it the practice after the חורבן.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'התקין' does NOT mean a rabbinic enactment. It means teaching a Torah law and putting it into practice.

phrases.english: What does 'instituted' mean?
He expounded the verse and established the practice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 4 and upholds Step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term in the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'התקין' means he expounded the Torah law and established it as practice after the חורבן.

steps.title: Originally, testimony about the new month was accepted all day
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. It describes the original practice: on the thirtieth day, בית דין accepted עדות החודש at any time during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: At first, בית דין would accept testimony about the new month for the entire day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us how things were done at first: witnesses who had seen the new moon could come and testify at any point during the thirtieth day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the starting point of the story. On the thirtieth day of אלול, nobody knew yet whether that day was ראש השנה. It depended on whether witnesses came. Originally there was no deadline: even witnesses arriving late in the day were accepted, and that day became ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. Marks the start of the משנה text.
Testimony from witnesses who saw the new moon. It is used to declare the new month.

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT a continuation of the יום הנף discussion from the earlier steps. It is a brand-new משנה about ראש השנה and קידוש החודש.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
phrases.notes: Marks the beginning of a new משנה.

phrases.english: Initially, they would accept
testimony of the new month the entire day.
phrases.notes: On the thirtieth day, witnesses could come at any hour.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ כׇּל הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It does not depend on the earlier יום הנף discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally, עדות החודש was accepted throughout the entire thirtieth day.

steps.title: Late witnesses caused the Levites to err, so testimony was limited to before afternoon
steps.stepSummary: One year the witnesses came late, and the לויים sang the wrong שיר. Because of this, the חכמים made a תקנה: testimony would be accepted only until מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once, the witnesses were delayed in coming, and the לויים made a mistake in the song. So the חכמים enacted that testimony would be accepted only until מנחה time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story that caused a change. Late witnesses created confusion in the בית המקדש, so the חכמים set a deadline of מנחה for accepting testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the afternoon תמיד, the לויים sang a שיר, and the song for ראש השנה is different from the song for a regular weekday. When the witnesses came very late, the לויים did not know which day it was, and the שיר went wrong. The משנה does not say exactly how; the גמרא asks this in Step 10. The fix was a deadline: if no witnesses came by מנחה, that day would not count as ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: They were delayed; they took a long time.
They got messed up; they made a mistake.
The לויים in the song they sing in the בית המקדש during the קרבן.
They (the חכמים) enacted a rule, a תקנה.
The time of the afternoon תמיד offering. This is the deadline set here.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic example of a rabbinic תקנה made to protect the proper service in the בית המקדש. Notice the word הִתְקִינוּ here. It really is a rabbinic enactment, which matches how the גמרא normally understood the word in Step 4.

phrases.english: Once, the witnesses were delayed in coming,
and the Levites erred in the song.
phrases.notes: They did not know whether to sing the weekday song or the ראש השנה song with the afternoon offering.

phrases.english: They instituted that they would not accept testimony
except until the time of minchah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes the original practice from Step 6 because of an incident.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the incident, testimony about the new month was accepted only until מנחה.

steps.title: Witnesses after afternoon: both days are kept holy
steps.stepSummary: If witnesses came after מנחה, people still treated that day as holy, and they also kept the next day holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if witnesses came from מנחה time and onward, people would treat that day as holy, and the next day as holy too.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what happens under the new rule when witnesses arrive too late, after the deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Officially, the next day becomes ראש השנה, and the coming יומים טובים are counted from it. Still, people kept the first day holy too, so that in future years they would not start working in the morning, assuming witnesses would only come late. The result is that both days were kept as קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy. Here it means treated as יום טוב.

steps.confusionAlert: The first day is kept holy only as a practice, so people would not treat it lightly. The official ראש השנה, used for counting the יומים טובים, is the second day.

phrases.english: And if witnesses came
from minchah time and onward,
they observe that day as holy,
phrases.notes: So that people would not get used to working on that day in future years.

phrases.english: and the next day as holy.
phrases.notes: The next day is the official ראש השנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם בָּאוּ עֵדִים מִן הַמִּנְחָה וּלְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what happens with late witnesses under the תקנה from Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses arriving after מנחה lead to both that day and the next day being kept holy.

steps.title: After the Temple's destruction, testimony was again accepted all day
steps.stepSummary: Once the בית המקדש was destroyed, there was no more שיר of the לויים to protect. So רבן יוחנן בן זכאי restored the original practice of accepting עדות החודש all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי enacted that they would accept testimony about the new month for the entire day.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by telling us that after the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי brought back the original rule from Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחה deadline existed only to prevent mistakes in the לויים' song in the בית המקדש. Once there was no בית המקדש, the reason was gone. So רבן יוחנן בן זכאי canceled the deadline, and testimony was again accepted all day.

keyTerms.meaning: He enacted or established a rule.
The great leader who rebuilt Torah life after the חורבן. He made several תקנות.

steps.whatToRemember: The full cycle: (1) testimony was accepted all day, (2) the deadline was limited to מנחה after the לויים erred, (3) witnesses after מנחה meant two holy days, (4) after the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי brought back all-day testimony, because the reason for the limit was gone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the well-known תקנות of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי after the חורבן. It shows a principle: when the reason for a תקנה no longer applies, it can be changed.

phrases.english: From when the Temple was destroyed,
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted
that they would accept testimony of the new month
the entire day.
phrases.notes: A return to the original practice from the start of the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Cancels the deadline from Step 7 and restores the original practice from Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי restored the acceptance of עדות החודש throughout the entire day.

steps.title: What exactly was the Levites' mistake?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the קלקול (mess-up) of the לויים in the שיר actually was.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What mistake did the לויים make with the song?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה by asking a simple clarifying question: what exactly did the לויים do wrong? This sets up two different answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said the לויים 'messed up' the שיר, without saying how. Since the witnesses came late in the day, the לויים did not yet know if today was ראש השנה. The גמרא wants to know what they actually did because of that doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Levites, who sang in the בית המקדש
The song the לויים sang with the קרבנות

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion of the משנה.

phrases.english: What mistake did the Levites make in the song?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of the משנה quoted in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What specific error the לויים made in the שיר on the day the witnesses came late.

steps.title: Babylonian view: they sang no song at all
steps.stepSummary: The Sages in בבל explained that the לויים did not sing any song at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here in בבל they explained: the לויים did not say any song at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer, from the Sages of בבל: the mistake was that the לויים were silent and sang nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לויים did not know whether to sing the regular weekday song or the special ראש השנה song. Because they were unsure, they sang nothing at all. In this view, the 'mistake' is leaving out the song entirely.

phrases.english: Here (in Babylonia) they explained:
that they did not say any song at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The לויים sang no song at all.

steps.title: רבי זירא: they sang the weekday song
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the mistake was singing the regular weekday song with the afternoon תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: they sang the weekday song with the afternoon תמיד.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives a second, different answer. The לויים did sing, but they sang the wrong song: the regular weekday one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the afternoon תמיד they assumed it was a regular day and sang the weekday song. When the witnesses then came and the day became ראש השנה, it turned out they should have sung the holiday song. So here the mistake is doing the wrong thing, not doing nothing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
that they said the song of a weekday
with the afternoon daily offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer that disagrees with Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The לויים sang the weekday song with the afternoon תמיד.

steps.title: רבי זירא sends a ברייתא to בבל
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells his son אהבה to teach the Babylonian Sages a ברייתא that says testimony was cut off so the song could be sung 'without a mistake.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to his son אהבה: Go out and teach them: They decreed that testimony about the new month would only be accepted if there was enough time left in the day to bring the תמידין, the מוספין, and their wine offerings, and to sing the song without a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings a ברייתא to support his view. This step sets up the source; the actual argument from it comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explains the reason for the תקנה from Step 7: there must be time to do the קרבנות and sing the song 'שלא בשיבוש', without a mistake. רבי זירא will focus on the word 'שיבוש'.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְאַהֲבָה בְּרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Ahava his son:
Go out and teach them (the Babylonian Sages):

phrases.aramaic: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ
phrases.english: They decreed that they would not accept testimony about the month
unless there would be enough time in the day
to offer the daily offerings, the additional offerings, and their libations,
and to say the song without a mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְאַהֲבָה בְּרֵיהּ פּוֹק תְּנִי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי זירא brings a source to support his answer in Step 12 against Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's view that the לויים sang the wrong (weekday) song.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says the song must be sung 'שלא בשיבוש'.

steps.title: The word 'mistake' fits only the weekday-song view
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא argues that 'שיבוש' means doing something wrong, which fits singing the weekday song, but not singing nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say they sang the weekday song, that is why there is a 'mistake.' But if you say they did not sing at all, what 'mistake' is there?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the argument from the ברייתא. It challenges the Babylonian view: the word 'mistake' does not seem to fit a case of simply not singing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'שיבוש' sounds like a wrong action, like singing the wrong song. If the לויים just stayed silent, that sounds like leaving something out, not a mix-up. So the wording seems to support רבי זירא.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא אֲמוּר שִׁירָה דְחוֹל —
phrases.english: It works well if you say they said the weekday song —
that is why there is a mistake.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לָא אֲמוּר כְּלָל —
phrases.english: But if you say they did not say (a song) at all —
what mistake is there?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Babylonian view (Step 11) that the לויים sang nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'שיבוש' implies doing something wrong, not leaving something out entirely.

steps.title: Singing nothing is the biggest mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: when no song is sung at all, there is no bigger mistake than that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they did not sing at all, there is no mistake greater than this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי זירא's proof. The word 'שיבוש' can also describe total silence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving out the song completely ruins the proper order of the עבודה even more than singing the wrong song. So the ברייתא's word 'mistake' fits both views, and the proof does not decide the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: There is nothing greater than this

steps.whatToRemember: At this point both views still stand: the Babylonian Sages say the לויים sang nothing, and רבי זירא says they sang the weekday song. The ברייתא's word 'שיבוש' fits either one. The next objection, from רב אחא בר הונא in Steps 16–19, challenges the Babylonian view.

phrases.english: Since they did not say (a song) at all —
you have no mistake greater than this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. It does not prove the Babylonian view is correct.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'שיבוש' must mean a wrong action. Total silence is an even bigger 'שיבוש'.

steps.title: רב אחא בר הונא brings the ראש השנה song list
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר הונא raises an objection from a ברייתא that lists the songs of ראש השנה: the morning תמיד as usual, 'הרנינו' for מוסף, and 'קול ה׳ יחיל מדבר' for מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר הונא objected: The morning תמיד of ראש השנה is offered in its usual way. With the מוסף, what do they say? 'Sing aloud to God our strength; shout to the God of יעקב.' With the מנחה, what do they say? 'The voice of ה׳ shakes the wilderness.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר הונא begins a new challenge by quoting a ברייתא about which songs were sung on ראש השנה. This step sets up the objection. The ברייתא continues in Steps 17–18, and Step 19 spells out its point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives each קרבן of ראש השנה its own song. In the morning the regular weekday song is used. מוסף gets 'הרנינו' (תהלים פ״א), and the afternoon תמיד gets a special song, 'קול ה׳ יחיל מדבר' (תהלים כ״ט). This list will be used to question the explanations given above.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קרב כהלכתו' does not mean nothing special happens on ראש השנה morning. It means the morning תמיד has its usual weekday song. The special songs come only with מוסף and מנחה.

phrases.english: Rav Aha bar Huna raised an objection:
The daily offering of Rosh HaShana in the morning
is offered according to its usual rules;
with the additional offering, what does one say?
"Sing aloud to God our strength;
shout to the God of Jacob" (Psalms 81:2);
with the afternoon offering, what does one say?
"The voice of the Lord shakes the wilderness" (Psalms 29:8).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new objection after the debate in Steps 11–15 ended without a decision.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Babylonian view (Step 11) that, when in doubt, the לויים sang no song at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Uses the ברייתא's fixed song list for ראש השנה as the basis for the challenge. The ברייתא continues in Steps 17–18, and Step 19 spells out the argument: 'repeating' the section implies the weekday song was sung while the day was in doubt.

steps.title: When Rosh Hashanah falls on Thursday, the morning song is changed to avoid repeating
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: on a Thursday ראש השנה, the regular Thursday song 'הרנינו' is not said in the morning, because it will be said at מוסף. Instead they sing the second half of that psalm, starting from 'הסירותי מסבל שכמו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: When ראש השנה falls on Thursday, whose regular song is 'Sing aloud to God our strength,' they would not say 'הרנינו' in the morning, because then they would be going back and repeating that section. So what do they say? 'I removed his shoulder from the burden.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא from Step 16. This part sets up the special Thursday case that the objection will depend on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ראש השנה, 'הרנינו' (תהילים פ״א) is sung for מוסף. Thursday's regular song is that same psalm. When the witnesses came before the morning תמיד, so the day was already known to be ראש השנה, they split the psalm to avoid singing it twice: the second half ('הסירותי') goes with the morning תמיד, and the first half ('הרנינו') goes with מוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: Thursday (the fifth day of the week)
'Sing aloud to God our strength' (Psalm 81), Thursday's regular song
going back and repeating the same section
'I removed his shoulder from the burden' (Psalm 81:7), the second half of the psalm

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT a new statement by the גמרא. It is the rest of the ברייתא that רב אחא בר הונא started quoting in Step 16. The objection itself comes in Step 19.

phrases.english: And when Rosh HaShanah falls
to be on Thursday,
whose regular song is
'Sing aloud to God our strength'
one would not say 'Sing aloud' in the morning,
because then one goes back and repeats the section.
phrases.notes: It will be sung again at מוסף

phrases.english: Rather, what does one say?
'I removed his shoulder from the burden.'
phrases.notes: The second half of the same psalm, about יוסף being freed on ראש השנה

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁחָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לִהְיוֹת בַּחֲמִישִׁי בַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא brought as the objection in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that, in a case of doubt, no song was sung at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This part sets up the Thursday case. The actual attack comes from the next clause and is spelled out in Step 19.

steps.title: If the witnesses came late, 'הרנינו' is repeated anyway
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if the witnesses arrived after the morning תמיד, they say 'הרנינו' at מוסף, even though this means repeating the section.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the witnesses came after the morning תמיד, one says 'הרנינו' at מוסף, even though one goes back and repeats the section.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the ברייתא, and it is the key line for the objection. When the witnesses came late, the psalm ends up being sung twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the witnesses came, nobody knew it was ראש השנה. Something was done with the song at the morning תמיד. The ברייתא calls singing 'הרנינו' at מוסף a 'repeat', which means 'הרנינו' was already sung in the morning.
steps.whyThisMatters: This clause is the evidence for רבי זירא. A 'repeat' requires that the weekday song was sung in the morning while the day's status was still unclear.

phrases.english: And if the witnesses came
after the morning daily offering,
one says 'Sing aloud' (at מוסף)

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחוֹזֵר וְכוֹפֵל אֶת הַפֶּרֶק.
phrases.english: even though one goes back and repeats the section.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם בָּאוּ עֵדִים אַחַר תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא and gives the late-witness case, which contrasts with the early-witness case in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that no song at all was sung in a case of doubt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling it a 'repeat' implies the weekday song 'הרנינו' was already sung with the morning תמיד.

steps.title: The repeat only makes sense if the weekday song was sung
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the objection. If, when in doubt, they sang the weekday song, then 'says it and repeats it' makes sense. But if they sang nothing at all, what is being repeated?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say that whenever there is a doubt, we sing the weekday song. That is why the ברייתא says 'one says it and repeats it.' But if you say no song is sung at all, what does 'one says it and repeats it' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out why the ברייתא is a problem. The word 'repeat' fits רבי זירא and challenges the view that no song was sung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a Thursday, the weekday song is 'הרנינו'. If it was sung in the morning during the doubt, singing it again at מוסף is truly a repeat. If nothing was sung in the morning, singing it at מוסף would be the first time, so the ברייתא's word 'repeat' would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: it works well if you say
they did not sing at all

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's phrase 'repeats the section' in the late-witness case shows that the weekday song was sung while the day was in doubt. This supports רבי זירא from Step 12.

phrases.english: It works well if you say
that anywhere there is a doubt
we sing the weekday song,
that is why it says:
'one says it and repeats it.'
But if you say
that they did not sing at all,
what does 'one says it and repeats it' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא quoted in Steps 16-18 works as an objection.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Babylonian view (Step 11, defended in Step 15) that the 'mistake' was singing no song at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 'repeat' requires that the song was already sung once. That only happens if the weekday song was sung in the morning during the doubt, which is רבי זירא's view.
